messages:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert: High 5xx rate observed on /v1/generate from edge-gateway-us-east-1 — impacted p95 latency and increased timeout errors. Escalation: paging oncall. severity: high :rotating_light:
oncall-ryan: Got the page, joining now. I can take triage. Can someone confirm customer-facing impact?
ops-jen: We're seeing a spike in 502/504 from the gateway. Dashboards show ~18% requests failing for the last 3 minutes. Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Some customers reporting timeouts.
maya: Confirming, we have inbound error spike and CQ in support reporting customer requests failing. Not a full outage but increased errors and timeouts.
infra-kate: Looking at infra metrics — egress retries to model-hosting cluster spiked at same time. Retries/sec up 5x. Connection errors to model-hosting pool nodes.
oncall-ryan: Ok — immediate steps: 1) put gateway on fallback route to smaller model cluster to reduce downstream load; 2) temporarily increase gateway retry limit/de-dup? 3) start log aggregation for correlation ids.
sam: Will open fallback route now. Executing: `infra route promote --from model-prod-eu --to model-fallback-us --selector gateway-route=/v1/generate`
sam: (bot) Route change accepted, rolling deploy to load balancers. Expect 10-20s to propagate.
ops-jen: Also increasing per-node connection pool size to model-hosting (temporary) — patch applied.
maya: I'm collecting traces. If you need specific correlation ids, query logs with: ```
kubectl logs -l app=gateway -n prod --since=15m | grep "cid="
# or via log-ql
logs.query("service:gateway AND cid:\"*") | filter status >= 500
```
infra-kate: Pulling sample correlation ids from error traces: cid=7f3a9d2b, cid=7f3a9d3c, cid=7f3a9d88. Attaching snippets.
maya: ```
[gateway] 2026-03-15T12:03:21Z cid=7f3a9d2b upstream=10.4.3.22:443 err=timeout backend_retries=3 latency=1280ms status=504
[gateway] 2026-03-15T12:03:22Z cid=7f3a9d3c upstream=10.4.5.18 err=connection_reset backend_retries=2 latency=940ms status=502
```
noncall-ryan: Good. Hypotheses so far: H1) upstream model-hosting cluster overloaded -> connection timeouts -> gateway retries amplify load. H2) model-hosting introduced a regression causing increased latency. H3) network egress throttling/SG misconfig. Let's track.
sre-bot: Incident channel created: #incident-2175556789. Runbooks suggested: apply route fallback, collect kvlogs, suspend non-essential background jobs.
ops-jen: I'm seeing increased 5xx correlated with a specific egress host pool (10.4.5.x). Could be one AZ degraded. Running `curl` healthcheck across nodes.
infra-kate: Healthchecks show 10.4.5.18 CPU pegged and thread pool saturated. Investigating process-level logs.
maya: Requesting team to avoid requeueing retries from clients — recommend lowering retry-attempts at gateway to 1 for this window to avoid amplification.
sam: Lowering gateway retry attempts via feature flag: `gateway.retries.max=1` -> applied to canary and rolling out.
oncall-ryan: Can we get a timeline: when did errors start, when did retries spike, when did fallback start?
maya: Timeline so far: 12:02 — first error increase at edge metrics. 12:03 — retries begin to climb. 12:04 — pager fired. 12:05 — route fallback initiated. 12:06 — gateway retry cap lowered. 12:08 — partial reduction in error rate but some customers still see timeouts.
sam: Route fallback completed at 12:07. Traffic shifted ~28% to fallback cluster.
ops-jen: Sharing logs for cid=7f3a9d88: ```
[ingress] cid=7f3a9d88 start
[gateway] cid=7f3a9d88 upstream=10.4.5.18 connect_timeout
[model-host] cid=7f3a9d88 queue=500ms exec=1200ms err=timeout
[gateway] cid=7f3a9d88 retries=3 status=504
```
infra-kate: Model-host logs show long GC pause around 12:02-12:04 on 10.4.5.18 — correlates with CPU spike. Could be memory churn after recent deploy.
maya: Any recent model-hosting deploys?
ops-jen: There was a canary deploy at 11:58 that rolled to the pool at 12:01. Ops notes show a small binary change to request parsing.
noncall-ryan: Flagging H2 (deploy regression) as high priority. Rolling back canary from 11:58 deploy on affected pool. Sam, can you trigger rollback for 10.4.5.*?
sam: Rolling back canary for that pool now -> `deploy rollback --id canary-20260315-1158 --targets 10.4.5.*` -> initiated.
ops-jen: Also disabling background batch jobs that hit model-hosting to reduce load. Done.
infra-kate: After rollback, GC pauses subside on 10.4.5.18, CPU back to normal by 12:12.
maya: Error rate dropped to ~3% by 12:14. Latency p95 improved. Looks like rollback mitigated.
oncall-ryan: Customer impact: partial, degraded for 12:02-12:14 window. Notify support and CS for tickets.
sre-bot: Next steps checklist: 1) postmortem ticket; 2) collect full kvlogs for cids 7f3a9d2b/3c/88; 3) add a pre-deploy load test for model-hosting canaries; 4) consider circuit-breaker at gateway to avoid retry amplification.
maya: Captured full kvlogs and traces and uploaded to artifact store: https://artifacts.internal/incident/2175556789/kvlogs.tar.gz
ops-jen: Filing RCA draft — initial root cause: canary deploy caused GC regressions on subset of model-hosting nodes leading to latency spikes -> gateway retries amplified load -> elevated 5xx/timeouts.
noncall-ryan: Thanks team. I'll mark incident as mitigated and start postmortem timeline doc. If anyone has more hypotheses or missed artifacts paste them here.
sam: Adding follow-ups in ticket: improve pre-deploy smoke tests, throttle gateway client retries by default, add sticky routing away from degraded AZs.
infra-kate: Also recommending alert tweak: alert on retry amplification ratio > 3x to catch this earlier.
maya: Noted. Closing handoff — moving to postmortem channel. :white_check_mark:
